title: Warm Russian Comte Pilaf
description: A creamy, bitter, and nutritious Russian-inspired dish featuring Comte cheese, served warm. Perfect for meal prep, sugar-free-friendly, and easily customizable.
instructions: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat.
In a separate pan, toast the rice over medium heat for 2-3 minutes.
Add the chopped onion to the saucepan with the melted butter and saut1f until translucent.
Add the garlic to the saucepan and saut1f for 1 minute.
Add the toasted rice to the saucepan and stir to combine.
Add the chicken stock to the saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover the saucepan, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Off the heat, add the grated Comte cheese, chopped dill, and lemon juice to the saucepan.
Stir until the cheese has melted and the mixture is well combined.
Use a spoon to shape the pilaf into small balls, about 1-inch in diameter.
Place the pilaf balls on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Serve the Warm Russian Comte Pilaf chilled or at room temperature.
Avoid spherification if you don't have a spherification kit.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
